rows.definition: Percentage of normal fuse-off complaints in cities and towns restored within the regulated time (DISCOM-wide).
rows.standard: Restore supply within 4 working hours of complaint (each case)

rows.interpretation: Direct comparison is not possible because the regulatory standard and reported performance use different measurement bases.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Connected-load-weighted frequency of sustained interruptions (each longer than 5 minutes) across 11 kV/33 kV feeders: SAIFI = sum(Ai x Ni) / Nt. rows.standard: Within the limits specified by the Authority in the Grid Connectivity Standards applicable to distribution systems (numerical limits not stated in the Regulations)
rows.reported_data: Sample compliance test: no deviations recorded against the limits stated in the return (LT 3.5%; HT 3.0%); no EHT samples; compliance percentage left blank.
rows.standardised_data: FY sample compliance with the limits stated in the return: 100.0% (LT and HT consumers).
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation refers to the limits in the Grid Connectivity Standards without stating them, and the limits used by DGVCL (3.5% LT, 3.0% HT/EHT) could not be matched to a published regulatory limit, so no like-for-like benchmark was established.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports no harmonics deviations in its sample tests, but the applicable regulatory limit could not be confirmed.
rows.documentation: Compliance share calculated as (sample size - deviations) / sample size, aggregated across LT and HT consumers; deviations were recorded as NIL.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Connected-load-weighted frequency of sustained interruptions (each longer than 5 minutes) across 11 kV/33 kV feeders: SAIFI = sum(Ai x Ni) / Nt. Computed monthly for the licensee as a whole by stacking 11 kV/33 kV feeders (excluding predominantly agricultural feeders); urban and rural feeders reported separately; agricultural feeders computed separately (cl. 7.3).
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; Commission to notify annual target levels (cl. 7.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Apr-22 3.37; May-22 5.39; Jun-22 5.80; Jul-22 6.81; Aug-22 5.52; Sep-22 5.39; Oct-22 3.57; Nov-22 3.19; Dec-22 3.30; Jan-23 4.60; Feb-23 2.50; Mar-23 3.15. Annual total row in the return: 4.38.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the October 2022 inputs on the SAIFI page conflict with the SAIDI and MAIFI pages, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for SAIFI (annual targets were to be notified by the Commission and none was identified for FY 2022-23); DGVCL's figures are also on a customers-served basis, not the connected-load basis by feeder segment in cl. 7.2.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly SAIFI ranged between 2.50 and 6.81 interruptions per consumer. The October 2022 inputs (customers served, customers affected, interruptions) differ from those on the other reliability pages, and the return's annual total row is an average monthly value, not an annual one.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be the sum of the 12 monthly indices (customer interruptions / customers served), but the October 2022 components cannot be reconciled across the return's pages and no month was estimated. The return's annual total row equals the average monthly value and was not used. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI)
rows.definition: Connected-load-weighted duration of sustained interruptions across 11 kV/33 kV feeders: SAIDI = sum(Bi x Ni) / Nt. Computed monthly for the licensee as a whole by stacking 11 kV/33 kV feeders (excluding predominantly agricultural feeders); urban and rural feeders reported separately; agricultural feeders computed separately (cl. 7.3). Unit of duration is not stated in the Regulations.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; Commission to notify annual target levels (cl. 7.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIDI (minutes per consumer): Apr-22 245 minutes; May-22 576 minutes; Jun-22 520 minutes; Jul-22 434 minutes; Aug-22 365 minutes; Sep-22 407 minutes; Oct-22 191 minutes; Nov-22 251 minutes; Dec-22 311 minutes; Jan-23 371 minutes; Feb-23 204 minutes; Mar-23 192 minutes. Annual total row in the return: 339 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the monthly components for October to December 2022 do not reproduce the reported monthly values, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for SAIDI (annual targets were to be notified by the Commission and none was identified for FY 2022-23); DGVCL's figures are also on a customers-served basis, not the connected-load basis by feeder segment in cl. 7.2.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly SAIDI ranged between about 3 and 10 hours per consumer. For October to December 2022 the reported values (03:11, 04:11, 05:11) do not follow from the customer-interruption hours shown in the return, and the return's annual total row is an average monthly value, not an annual one.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be the sum of the 12 monthly indices (cumulative customer-interruption hours / customers served), but three months do not reconcile and no month was estimated. The return's annual total row equals the average monthly value and was not used. | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours:minutes (hh:mm) to minutes for consistency across all DISCOMs and states (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '04:05' -> '245 minutes'; '09:36' -> '576 minutes'; '08:40' -> '520 minutes'; '07:14' -> '434 minutes'; '06:05' -> '365 minutes'; '06:47' -> '407 minutes'; '03:11' -> '191 minutes'; '04:11' -> '251 minutes'; '05:11' -> '311 minutes'; '06:11' -> '371 minutes'; '03:24' -> '204 minutes'; '03:12' -> '192 minutes'; '05:39' -> '339 minutes'.

rows.indicator: Complaints redressed within stipulated time: class A(i) (Interruption in supply: loose connections from pole)
rows.definition: Share of complaints of Appendix-A class A(i) (Interruption in supply: loose connections from pole) redressed within the stipulated time, as compiled in the complaint register prescribed in Appendix-B (monthly, reported quarterly).
rows.standard: Each complaint redressed within the time stipulated in the Regulations for its type
rows.reported_data: Within-stipulated-time share: Q1 100.0%; Q2 100.0%; Q3 100.0%; Q4 100.0%.
rows.standardised_data: FY within-stipulated-time share: 100.0%.
rows.why_not_comparable: The standards are time limits for each individual complaint (varying by area, fault type or load), while DGVCL reports only an aggregate share of complaints in this class redressed within the stipulated time.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports all complaints of this class as redressed within the stipulated time, 28.1% of them within half of it. These are self-reported class-level aggregates.
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares calculated as (redressed within 50% + within stipulated time) / total complaints. FY share calculated from summed quarterly numerators and denominators; quarterly percentages were not averaged.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Connected-load-weighted frequency of sustained interruptions (each longer than 5 minutes) across 11 kV/33 kV feeders: SAIFI = sum(Ai x Ni) / Nt. rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets by separate order (SoP 2005 cl. 7.4; SoP 2023 cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Apr-23 4.22; May-23 3.74; Jun-23 6.99; Jul-23 5.13; Aug-23 3.65; Sep-23 4.59; Oct-23 4.22; Nov-23 3.13; Dec-23 3.41; Jan-24 4.36; Feb-24 2.55; Mar-24 2.38. Annual total row in the return: 4.19.

The return's annual total row equals neither the sum nor the simple average of the monthly values and was not used.

rows.indicator: Complaints redressed within stipulated time: class A(i) (Interruption in supply: loose connections from pole)
rows.definition: Share of complaints of class A(i) (Interruption in supply: loose connections from pole) redressed within the stipulated time, as compiled in the complaint register of the Performa SoP 003 B (SoP 2005 Appendix-A/B classes; monthly, reported quarterly). The return uses these classes for the whole year, including the period from 6 December 2023.
rows.standard: Each complaint redressed within the time stipulated in the Regulations in force for its type (SoP Regulations 2005 to 5 December 2023; SoP Regulations 2023 from 6 December 2023)
rows.reported_data: Within-stipulated-time share: Q1 100.0%; Q2 100.0%; Q3 100.0%; Q4 100.0%.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the quarter III entries are identical to quarter II in every class, so a reliable four-quarter value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The standards are time limits for each individual complaint (varying by area, fault type or load, and changed for several complaint types on 6 December 2023), while DGVCL reports only an aggregate share of complaints in this class redressed within the stipulated time, for quarters that straddle the change of regulation.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports every complaint of this class as redressed within the stipulated time in each quarter. The quarter III entries repeat the quarter II entries exactly, which raises doubt about the quarter III data. These are self-reported class-level aggregates.
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares calculated as (redressed within 50% + within stipulated time) / total complaints. A four-quarter FY share was not constructed because the quarter III block duplicates quarter II; no quarter was estimated or replaced.

rows.why_not_comparable: The standards are time limits for each individual complaint (varying by area, fault type or load, and changed for several complaint types on 6 December 2023), while DGVCL reports only an aggregate share of complaints in this class redressed within the stipulated time, for quarters that straddle the change of regulation.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports every complaint of this class as redressed within the stipulated time in each quarter. The quarter III entries repeat the quarter II entries exactly, which raises doubt about the quarter III data. These are self-reported class-level aggregates.
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares calculated as (redressed within 50% + within stipulated time) / total complaints. A four-quarter FY share was not constructed because the quarter III block duplicates quarter II; no quarter was estimated or replaced.

rows.indicator: Replacement of defective meter – % within time limit
rows.definition: Share of complaints of class C(i) (Meters: stopped or defective meters) redressed within the stipulated time, as compiled in the complaint register of the Performa SoP 003 B (SoP 2005 Appendix-A/B classes; monthly, reported quarterly). The return uses these classes for the whole year, including the period from 6 December 2023.
rows.standard: Each complaint redressed within the time stipulated in the Regulations in force for its type (SoP Regulations 2005 to 5 December 2023; SoP Regulations 2023 from 6 December 2023)
rows.reported_data: Within-stipulated-time share: Q1 100.0%; Q2 100.0%; Q3 100.0%; Q4 100.0%.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the quarter III entries are identical to quarter II in every class, so a reliable four-quarter value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The standards are time limits for each individual complaint (varying by area, fault type or load, and changed for several complaint types on 6 December 2023), while DGVCL reports only an aggregate share of complaints in this class redressed within the stipulated time, for quarters that straddle the change of regulation.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports every complaint of this class as redressed within the stipulated time in each quarter. The quarter III entries repeat the quarter II entries exactly, which raises doubt about the quarter III data. These are self-reported class-level aggregates.
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares calculated as (redressed within 50% + within stipulated time) / total complaints. A four-quarter FY share was not constructed because the quarter III block duplicates quarter II; no quarter was estimated or replaced. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Complaints redressed within stipulated time: class C(i) (Meters: stopped or defective meters)'.

rows.indicator_family: Temporary supply - refund of balance deposit
rows.indicator: Refund of balance deposit after temporary supply – Class G, % within time limit
rows.definition: Share of complaints of class G (Refund of amount due on temporary connection) redressed within the stipulated time, as compiled in the complaint register of the Performa SoP 003 B (SoP 2005 Appendix-A/B classes; monthly, reported quarterly). The return uses these classes for the whole year, including the period from 6 December 2023.
rows.standard: Each complaint redressed within the time stipulated in the Regulations in force for its type (SoP Regulations 2005 to 5 December 2023; SoP Regulations 2023 from 6 December 2023)
rows.reported_data: Within-stipulated-time share: Q1 100.0%; Q2 100.0%; Q3 100.0%; Q4 100.0%.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the quarter III entries are identical to quarter II in every class, so a reliable four-quarter value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The standards are time limits for each individual complaint (varying by area, fault type or load, and changed for several complaint types on 6 December 2023), while DGVCL reports only an aggregate share of complaints in this class redressed within the stipulated time, for quarters that straddle the change of regulation.
rows.interpretation: DGVCL reports every complaint of this class as redressed within the stipulated time in each quarter. The quarter III entries repeat the quarter II entries exactly, which raises doubt about the quarter III data. These are self-reported class-level aggregates.
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares calculated as (redressed within 50% + within stipulated time) / total complaints. A four-quarter FY share was not constructed because the quarter III block duplicates quarter II; no quarter was estimated or replaced. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Complaints redressed within stipulated time: class G (Refund of amount due on temporary connection)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions per consumer: SAIFI = number of interrupted consumers for sustained interruption events / total consumers served = sum(Ai x Ni) / Nt (IEEE 1366-2003). Computed monthly for the licensee as a whole by stacking all 11 kV/33 kV feeders, excluding those serving predominantly agricultural loads, and aggregating the number and duration of interruptions per feeder; an outage of 5 minutes or less is momentary, longer is sustained; scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages are excluded (cl. 5.1-5.2). Maintained by zone/circle/division/sub-division and for urban and rural areas separately; agricultural feeders computed separately.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Apr-24 3.18; May-24 5.43; Jun-24 6.68; Jul-24 8.39; Aug-24 8.29; Sep-24 8.48; Oct-24 10.68; Nov-24 4.92; Dec-24 5.60; Jan-25 5.83; Feb-25 3.90; Mar-25 5.27. Annual total row in the return: 6.39.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: for Jun-24, Jul-24, Sep-24, Jan-25 the SAIFI page conflicts with the SAIDI and MAIFI pages on customers served, interruptions or customers affected, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for SAIFI (the Commission was to set base/target indices by separate order and none was identified for FY 2024-25); DGVCL's figures are also on a customers-served basis for the whole licensee, not split by urban and rural feeders as the regulation requires.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly SAIFI ranged between 3.18 and 10.68 interruptions per consumer, peaking in October 2024. For Jun-24, Jul-24, Sep-24, Jan-25 the inputs differ from those on the other reliability pages. The return's annual total row equals the simple average of the monthly values.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be the sum of the 12 monthly indices (customer interruptions / customers served), but the inputs for Jun-24, Jul-24, Sep-24, Jan-25 conflict across the return's pages and no month was estimated. The return's annual total row is shown for reference and was not used as the FY figure. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)'.

rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI)
rows.definition: Average time to restore service for consumers who experienced a sustained interruption: CAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration / total number of interrupted consumers = SAIDI / SAIFI (cl. 5.2(III)); to be computed separately for HT consumers from metering data. Computed monthly on the same stacked 11 kV/33 kV feeder basis as SAIFI.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly CAIDI (minutes): Apr-24 40 minutes; May-24 42 minutes; Jun-24 36 minutes; Jul-24 38 minutes; Aug-24 38 minutes; Sep-24 36 minutes; Oct-24 40 minutes; Nov-24 41 minutes; Dec-24 38 minutes; Jan-25 39 minutes; Feb-25 41 minutes; Mar-25 40 minutes. Annual total row in the return: 39 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: no month's reported CAIDI can be reproduced from the SAIDI and SAIFI pages, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for CAIDI (the Commission was to set base/target indices by separate order and none was identified for FY 2024-25); DGVCL reports one licensee-wide series and no separate CAIDI for HT consumers, which the regulation also requires.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly CAIDI ranged between 36 and 42 minutes. CAIDI should equal SAIDI divided by SAIFI, but the cumulative interruption duration on the SAIDI page divided by the customer interruptions on the SAIFI page gives 32 to 63 minutes depending on the month, and the 'total restoration time' column on the CAIDI page does not match the SAIDI page. The return's annual total row equals the simple average of the monthly values.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be cumulative customer interruption duration / total customer interruptions over the 12 months, but the reported monthly values do not follow from the components in the return. No month was estimated or repaired. The return's annual total row is shown for reference and was not used as the FY figure. | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours:minutes (hh:mm) to minutes for consistency across all DISCOMs and states (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '00:40' -> '40 minutes'; '00:42' -> '42 minutes'; '00:36' -> '36 minutes'; '00:38' -> '38 minutes'; '00:38' -> '38 minutes'; '00:36' -> '36 minutes'; '00:40' -> '40 minutes'; '00:41' -> '41 minutes'; '00:38' -> '38 minutes'; '00:39' -> '39 minutes'; '00:41' -> '41 minutes'; '00:40' -> '40 minutes'; '00:39' -> '39 minutes'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions per consumer: SAIFI = number of interrupted consumers for sustained interruption events / total consumers served = sum(Ai x Ni) / Nt (IEEE 1366-2003). Computed monthly for the licensee as a whole by stacking all 11 kV/33 kV feeders, excluding those serving predominantly agricultural loads, and aggregating the number and duration of interruptions per feeder; an outage of 5 minutes or less is momentary, longer is sustained; scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages are excluded (cl. 5.1-5.2). Maintained by zone/circle/division/sub-division and for urban and rural areas separately; agricultural feeders computed separately.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Apr-25 5.10; May-25 14.14; Jun-25 13.10; Jul-25 8.83; Aug-25 8.21; Sep-25 7.57; Oct-25 5.26; Nov-25 3.57; Dec-25 3.39; Jan-26 3.73; Feb-26 1.84; Mar-26 3.05. Annual total row in the return: 7.46.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: for May-25 the SAIFI page conflicts with the SAIDI page on the number of sustained interruptions, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for SAIFI (the Commission was to set base/target indices by separate order and none was identified for FY 2025-26); DGVCL's figures are also on a customers-served basis for the whole licensee, not split by urban and rural feeders as the regulation requires.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly SAIFI ranged between 1.84 and 14.14 interruptions per consumer, peaking in May-25. For May-25 the number of sustained interruptions differs between the SAIFI page (and the CAIDI page) and the SAIDI page. The return's annual total row (7.46) is neither the sum (77.79) nor the simple average (6.48) of the monthly values.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be the sum of the 12 monthly indices (customer interruptions / customers served), but the interruption count for May-25 conflicts across the return's pages and no month was estimated or repaired. The return's annual total row is shown for reference and was not used as the FY figure. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)'.

rows.indicator: Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index (MAIFI) – Connected-load basis
rows.definition: Average number of momentary interruptions per consumer: MAIFI = cumulative momentary customer interruptions / total consumers served = sum(Imi x Nmi) / Nt (IEEE 1366-2003). Computed monthly for the licensee as a whole by stacking all 11 kV/33 kV feeders, excluding those serving predominantly agricultural loads, and aggregating the number and duration of interruptions per feeder; an outage of 5 minutes or less is momentary, longer is sustained; scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages are excluded (cl. 5.1-5.2). Maintained by zone/circle/division/sub-division and for urban and rural areas separately; agricultural feeders computed separately.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly MAIFI (momentary interruptions per consumer): Apr-25 6.35; May-25 13.55; Jun-25 13.61; Jul-25 10.60; Aug-25 9.44; Sep-25 8.07; Oct-25 7.01; Nov-25 4.45; Dec-25 3.93; Jan-26 3.98; Feb-26 2.34; Mar-26 3.28. Annual total row in the return: 8.25.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: the monthly inputs for Jul-25 conflict across pages.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for MAIFI (the Commission was to set base/target indices by separate order and none was identified for FY 2025-26); DGVCL's figures are also on a customers-served basis for the whole licensee, not split by urban and rural feeders as the regulation requires.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly MAIFI ranged between 2.34 and 13.61 momentary interruptions per consumer, peaking in Jun-25. Each month's components reproduce the reported value; for Jul-25 its customers-served figure differs from the SAIDI and SAIFI pages. The return's annual total row (8.25) is neither the sum (86.61) nor the simple average (7.22) of the monthly values.
rows.documentation: FY value not constructed: the annual figure would be the sum of the 12 monthly indices (cumulative momentary customer interruptions / customers served), but customers served for Jul-25 differs between the MAIFI page and the SAIDI and SAIFI pages and no month was estimated or repaired. The return's annual total row is shown for reference and was not used as the FY figure. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index (MAIFI)'.

rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI)
rows.definition: Average time to restore service for consumers who experienced a sustained interruption: CAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration / total number of interrupted consumers = SAIDI / SAIFI (cl. 5.2(III)); to be computed separately for HT consumers from metering data. Computed monthly on the same stacked 11 kV/33 kV feeder basis as SAIFI.
rows.standard: No numerical target in the Regulations; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (cl. 5.4)
rows.reported_data: Monthly CAIDI (minutes): Apr-25 43 minutes; May-25 31 minutes; Jun-25 30 minutes; Jul-25 38 minutes; Aug-25 34 minutes; Sep-25 35 minutes; Oct-25 35 minutes; Nov-25 51 minutes; Dec-25 48 minutes; Jan-26 37 minutes; Feb-26 35 minutes; Mar-26 48 minutes. Annual total row in the return: 49 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: for May-25 the interruption count conflicts between the SAIFI and SAIDI pages, so a valid 12-month value cannot be built.
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulation sets no numerical benchmark for CAIDI (the Commission was to set base/target indices by separate order and none was identified for FY 2025-26); DGVCL reports one licensee-wide series and no separate CAIDI for HT consumers, which the regulation also requires.
rows.interpretation: Reported monthly CAIDI ranged between 30 and 51 minutes. Every month's reported value is within one minute of the cumulative interruption duration on the SAIDI page divided by the customer interruptions on the SAIFI page (the return truncates to the minute). For May-25 the interruption count differs between the SAIFI and SAIDI pages. The return's annual total row (00:49) is not the simple average of the monthly values (00:38).

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)
rows.definition: Average number of sustained 11 kV-feeder interruptions per consumer in the licensee area: SAIFI = sum over 11 kV feeders of (interruptions on feeder x consumers on feeder) / total consumers on all feeders, for the quarter or half-year.
rows.standard: Not more than 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter (20 per six months)
rows.reported_data: SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Q1 2.25; Q2 3.12; Q3 2.62; Q4 2.48.
rows.standardised_data: FY SAIFI: 10.47 interruptions per consumer.
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.why_not_comparable: Not applicable (comparison possible).
rows.interpretation: Every quarter was within the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter; the highest was Q2 (3.12). The annual figure is for presentation and is not compared with the quarterly limit. The DISCOM totals printed in the returns cannot be reproduced as a consumer-weighted average of the zone-level figures in the same returns, so the reported level should be read with caution; the result against the limit is the same on either basis.
rows.documentation: FY index = sum of the four quarterly index values weighted by each quarter's consumer base, divided by the mean consumer base of the four quarters (sum of quarterly consumer-interruptions / mean consumers). DISCOM-level quarterly values as reported; monthly data were not reported. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

SAIDI is printed in minutes in the returns and has been converted to hours.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)
rows.definition: Average number of sustained 11 kV-feeder interruptions per consumer in the licensee area: SAIFI = sum over 11 kV feeders of (interruptions on feeder x consumers on feeder) / total consumers on all feeders, for the quarter or half-year.
rows.standard: Not more than 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter (20 per six months)
rows.reported_data: SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Q1 4.46; Q2 4.46; Q3 2.99; Q4 2.74.
rows.standardised_data: FY SAIFI: 14.55 interruptions per consumer.
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.why_not_comparable: Not applicable (comparison possible).
rows.interpretation: Every quarter was within the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter; the highest was Q1 (4.46). The annual figure is for presentation and is not compared with the quarterly limit. The DISCOM totals printed in the returns cannot be reproduced as a consumer-weighted average of the zone-level figures in the same returns, so the reported level should be read with caution; the result against the limit is the same on either basis.
rows.documentation: FY index = sum of the four quarterly index values weighted by each quarter's consumer base, divided by the mean consumer base of the four quarters (sum of quarterly consumer-interruptions / mean consumers). DISCOM-level quarterly values as reported; monthly data were not reported. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI)
rows.definition: Average duration of sustained 11 kV-feeder interruptions per consumer in the licensee area: SAIDI = sum over 11 kV feeders of (duration of interruptions on feeder x consumers on feeder) / total consumers on all feeders, for the quarter or half-year.
rows.standard: Not more than 15 hours per consumer per quarter (30 hours per six months)
rows.reported_data: SAIDI (minutes per consumer, as printed in the returns): Q1 117.6; Q2 146.4; Q3 86.4; Q4 74.4.
rows.standardised_data: FY SAIDI: 421.2 minutes per consumer.
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.why_not_comparable: Not applicable (comparison possible).
rows.interpretation: Every quarter was within the limit of 15 hours per consumer per quarter; the highest was Q2 (2.44). The annual figure is for presentation and is not compared with the quarterly limit. The DISCOM totals printed in the returns cannot be reproduced as a consumer-weighted average of the zone-level figures in the same returns, so the reported level should be read with caution; the result against the limit is the same on either basis. SAIDI is printed in minutes in the returns and has been converted to hours.
rows.documentation: FY index = sum of the four quarterly index values weighted by each quarter's consumer base, divided by the mean consumer base of the four quarters (sum of quarterly consumer-interruptions / mean consumers). DISCOM-level quarterly values as reported; monthly data were not reported. Unit conversion: the returns print SAIDI in minutes; each quarterly value was divided by 60 to give hours, the unit in which the standard is stated (no other transformation). | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index)'. | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours to minutes (the unit used for SAIDI throughout the dataset); the unit was given as a label rather than beside each value. Original values: Q1 1.96 h -> 117.6 min; Q2 2.44 h -> 146.4 min; Q3 1.44 h -> 86.4 min; Q4 1.24 h -> 74.4 min. | Unit conversion: standardised value converted to minutes (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '7.02 hours' -> '421.2 minutes'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 15 hours per consumer per quarter in the Standard (900 minutes)); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions per consumer in the quarter across the licensee area, SAIFI = Σ(Ai·Ni) ÷ Nt over 11 kV feeders (reg. 3; Schedule I cl. 2.3). Unit: interruptions per consumer.
rows.standard: Not more than 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter (20 per six months)
rows.reported_data: Licensee-wide SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Q1 5.35; Q2 5.08; Q3 4.15; Q4 3.92
rows.standardised_data: FY 2021-22 SAIFI: 18.48 interruptions per consumer (sum of the four quarters)
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.interpretation: Licensee-wide SAIFI was below 10 in every quarter (highest 5.35). Circle-level values were above 10 in some circles in some quarters; the standard applies to the licensee-wide index.
rows.documentation: Licensee-wide values are consumer-weighted averages of the circle-level SAIFI in the licensee's resubmitted ('Revised') SOP-2C tables, matching the formula in Schedule I (Σ Ni·index ÷ Nt). The 'Total' row printed in those tables is an unweighted mean of circles and is not used. FY SAIFI = sum over Q1–Q4 of circle consumers × SAIFI ÷ mean quarterly consumers. The standard remains quarterly. Q4 feeder counts for four circles are shown as zero in the source (consumer counts complete). | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index, SAIFI (quarterly)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) – Quarterly
rows.definition: Average duration of sustained interruptions per consumer in the quarter across the licensee area, SAIDI = Σ(Bi·Ni) ÷ Nt over 11 kV feeders (reg. 3; Schedule I cl. 2.3). Unit: hours per consumer.
rows.standard: Not more than 15 hours per consumer per quarter (30 hours per six months)
rows.reported_data: Licensee-wide SAIDI (minutes per consumer): Q1 327; Q2 367.2; Q3 311.4; Q4 271.2
rows.standardised_data: FY 2021-22 SAIDI: 1,276.2 minutes per consumer (sum of the four quarters)
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.interpretation: Licensee-wide SAIDI was below 15 hours in every quarter (highest 6.12). Several circles reported values above 15 hours in some quarters; the standard applies to the licensee-wide index.
rows.documentation: Licensee-wide values are consumer-weighted averages of circle-level SAIDI from the resubmitted ('Revised') SOP-2C tables (Σ Ni·index ÷ Nt). The printed 'Total' row (an unweighted mean) is not used. FY SAIDI = sum over Q1–Q4 of circle consumers × SAIDI ÷ mean quarterly consumers. The standard remains quarterly. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Duration Index, SAIDI (quarterly)'. | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours to minutes (the unit used for SAIDI throughout the dataset); the unit was given as a label rather than beside each value. Original values: Q1 5.45 h -> 327 min; Q2 6.12 h -> 367.2 min; Q3 5.19 h -> 311.4 min; Q4 4.52 h -> 271.2 min. | Unit conversion: standardised value converted to minutes (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '21.27 hours' -> '1,276.2 minutes'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 15 hours per consumer per quarter in the Standard (900 minutes)); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.indicator: Supply restoration after no-current complaint – % within time limit
rows.definition: Percentage of no-current complaints (supply restoration) (brought forward plus received in the quarter) redressed within the Schedule I time limit, as reported by the licensee in format SOP-2A. Unit: % of complaints. Schedule I limit: restoration within 2 hours (Class-1 cities), 4 hours (urban), 8 hours (rural) of reporting.
rows.standard: Schedule III: at least 95% of cases redressed within the Schedule I time limit, assessed each quarter
rows.standardised_data: FY 2023-24 within-time share: 99.32%
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.interpretation: The within-time share was at or above the 95% minimum in every quarter; the lowest quarterly share was 98.96% (Q1).
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares are as reported (redressed in time ÷ [brought forward + received]) and were re-derived from the underlying counts. The FY share is redressed in time over Q1–Q4 ÷ (opening balance at start of Q1 + complaints received in Q1–Q4), so carried-forward complaints are counted once; quarterly percentages are not averaged. The standard is not transformed and is assessed on its quarterly basis. The Q4 report prints the shares as whole numbers; the Q4 share shown here is re-derived from the printed counts. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Share of no-current complaints (supply restoration) redressed within the prescribed time (quarterly)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's within-time share compared with the 95% minimum in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.standard: Not more than 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter (20 per six months)

rows.interpretation: Licensee-wide SAIFI was within the limit of 10 in every quarter (highest 4.12). Circle-level SAIFI was above 10 in 7 circle-quarters; the standard applies to the licensee-wide index.
rows.documentation: Licensee-wide values are consumer-weighted averages of the circle-level SAIFI in the licensee's SOP-2C tables, matching the formula in Schedule I (Σ Ni·index ÷ Nt). The 'Total' row printed in those tables equals an unweighted mean of circles in Q1–Q2 but cannot be reproduced from the circle rows in Q3–Q4, and is not used. rows.indicator: Supply restoration after no-current complaint – % within time limit
rows.definition: Percentage of no-current complaints (supply restoration) (brought forward plus received in the quarter) redressed within the Schedule I time limit, as reported by the licensee in format SOP-2A. Unit: % of complaints. Schedule I limit: restoration within 2 hours (Class-1 cities), 4 hours (urban), 8 hours (rural) of reporting.
rows.standard: Schedule III: at least 95% of cases redressed within the Schedule I time limit, assessed each quarter
rows.standardised_data: FY 2024-25 within-time share: 98.55%
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: No (FY: No)
rows.interpretation: The within-time share fell below the 95% minimum in at least one quarter; lowest 94.91% (Q4).
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares are as reported (redressed in time ÷ [brought forward + received]) and were re-derived from the underlying counts. Quarterly percentages are not averaged. The standard is not transformed and is assessed on its quarterly basis. The licensee prints the shares as whole numbers; the quarterly shares shown here are re-derived from the printed counts (redressed in time ÷ total complaints). The FY share pools the four quarters (sum of redressals in time ÷ sum of the quarterly total complaints), so a complaint carried forward from one quarter can appear in more than one quarterly total. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Share of no-current complaints (supply restoration) redressed within the prescribed time (quarterly)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's within-time share compared with the 95% minimum in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

Unit: % of complaints. Schedule I limit: restoration within 2 hours (Class-1 cities), 4 hours (urban), 8 hours (rural) of reporting.
rows.standard: Schedule III: at least 95% of cases redressed within the Schedule I time limit, assessed each quarter
rows.standardised_data: FY 2025-26 within-time share: 98.87%
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.interpretation: The within-time share was at or above the 95% minimum in every quarter; the lowest quarterly share was 97.67% (Q1).
rows.documentation: Quarterly shares are as reported (redressed in time ÷ [brought forward + received]) and were re-derived from the underlying counts. Quarterly percentages are not averaged. The standard is not transformed and is assessed on its quarterly basis. The licensee prints the shares as whole numbers; the quarterly shares shown here are re-derived from the printed counts (redressed in time ÷ total complaints). The FY share pools the four quarters (sum of redressals in time ÷ sum of the quarterly total complaints), so a complaint carried forward from one quarter can appear in more than one quarterly total. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Quarterly
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions per consumer in the quarter across the licensee area, SAIFI = Σ(Ai·Ni) ÷ Nt over 11 kV feeders (reg. 3; Schedule I cl. 2.3). Unit: interruptions per consumer.
rows.standard: Not more than 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter (20 per six months)
rows.reported_data: Licensee-wide SAIFI (interruptions per consumer): Q1 3.34; Q2 3.26; Q3 3.17; Q4 3.20
rows.standardised_data: FY 2025-26 SAIFI: 12.98 interruptions per consumer (sum of the four quarters)
rows.standard_met_detail: Q1: Yes, Q2: Yes, Q3: Yes, Q4: Yes (FY: Yes)
rows.interpretation: Licensee-wide SAIFI was within the limit of 10 in every quarter (highest 3.34). Circle-level SAIFI was above 10 in 0 circle-quarters; the standard applies to the licensee-wide index.
rows.documentation: Licensee-wide values are consumer-weighted averages of the circle-level SAIFI in the licensee's SOP-2C tables, matching the formula in Schedule I (Σ Ni·index ÷ Nt). The 'Total' row printed in those tables cannot be reproduced from the circle rows in any quarter (neither as an unweighted mean nor consumer-weighted) and is not used. The licensee reports 14 circles in every quarter (a note on each SOP-2C page states that the Anoopgarh and Sanchore O&M circles were abolished and merged into Sriganganagar and Jalore); weights are each quarter's own circle consumer counts. FY SAIFI = sum over Q1–Q4 of circle consumers × SAIFI ÷ mean quarterly consumer base. The standard remains quarterly. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index, SAIFI (quarterly)'. | Standard met? expanded to quarterly verdicts (each quarter's value compared with the limit of 10 interruptions per consumer per quarter in the Standard); FY verdict unchanged.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 011-A format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-interruptions divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 011-A reporting format.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; Commission to notify annual targets (Reg. 7.4).
rows.reported_data: 3.79 interruptions per customer per month (monthly average as printed in the return).
rows.standardised_data: 45.58 interruptions per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders or load-weighted as Regulation 7.2 prescribes.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard.
rows.documentation: The return's 3.79 is the total of the twelve monthly numerators divided by the total of the twelve monthly customer counts, a customer-weighted monthly average (the simple mean of the monthly indices is 3.80). Annual SAIFI = sum over months of (customer interruptions / customers served) = 45.58, computed from each month's own figures. Monthly indices were recomputed from the return's numerators and denominators and agree with the printed values to two decimals. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 011-A format)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 011-A format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-interruptions divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 011-A reporting format (the definition in 2023 Reg. 5.2).
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets (2005 Reg. 7.4; 2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: 4.84 interruptions per customer per month (monthly average as printed in the return).
rows.standardised_data: 58.18 interruptions per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard.
rows.documentation: The return's 4.84 is the total of the twelve monthly numerators divided by the total of the twelve monthly customer counts, a customer-weighted monthly average. Annual SAIFI = sum over months of (customer interruptions / customers served), computed from each month's own figures. Monthly indices recomputed from the return agree with the printed values to two decimals. The customer-count basis matches the 2023 definition; the 2005 definition is load-weighted. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 011-A format)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: SAIFI = sum of (Ai x Ni) / Nt, where Ai = sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) on the ith 11 kV/33 kV feeder in the month, Ni = connected load of the ith feeder affected by each interruption, Nt = total connected load at 11 kV in the licensed area. Computed for the licensee as a whole; feeders segregated into rural and urban and reported separately each month.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations. rows.indicator: Complaints redressed within stipulated time - class A(i): Interruption in power supply - loose connections at meter, MCB or service line or from pole
rows.definition: Share of complaints of class A(i) redressed within the time stipulated in the Regulations, per the licensee's complaint-register classification (Appendix A of the 2023 Regulations).
rows.standard: Each complaint redressed within the stipulated time for its class.
rows.reported_data: 98.68% of complaints redressed within the stipulated time.
rows.standardised_data: 98.68% (annual register; no annualisation required).
rows.why_not_comparable: Not applicable: comparison is possible.
rows.interpretation: 3,680 of 278,140 complaints (1.32%) in this class were redressed beyond the stipulated time, whereas the standard requires every complaint to be redressed within it. The figure is self-reported and not independently audited.
rows.documentation: Share = complaints redressed within the stipulated time / total complaints, from the annual register: 274,460 / 278,140. Nothing was pending at the start or end of the year. The register has a single within/beyond split (no time bands), so no further adjustment was needed.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 010 format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-interruptions divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 010 reporting format (the definition in 2023 Reg. 5.2).
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: 10.61 interruptions per customer per month (monthly average as printed in the return).
rows.standardised_data: 127.50 interruptions per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard. The annual figure is more than double the FY 2023-24 annual figure (58.18), while the annual SAIDI is far lower; see Source_Gaps G18.
rows.documentation: The return's 10.61 is the total of the twelve monthly numerators divided by the total of the twelve monthly customer counts, a customer-weighted monthly average and not an annual value. Annual SAIFI = sum over months of (customer interruptions / customers served), each month with its own customer count. The monthly indices agree with the printed values to two decimals. The numerator is the figure in column 6 of the SoP 010 table, which is labelled 'sum of (3 x 4)' but does not equal the product of the printed columns 3 and 4; it was used because it reproduces the printed monthly index. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 010 format)'.
rows.applicable_regulation: Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standards of Performance of Distribution Licensees) Regulations, 2023 (Notification No. 2 of 2023; Gujarat Government Gazette Extraordinary No. 108, Part IV-C, 06-12-2023)
rows.reported_data_source: MGVCL Standards of Performance return, FY 2024-25 (annual; file 'FY_2024-25_6.pdf') (Madhya Gujarat Vij Company Limited (as submitted under the Regulations), 2024-25)

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 011 format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-minutes of interruption divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 011 reporting format.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: 26.8 minutes per customer per month (monthly average; printed in the return as 0:26 hr:min).
rows.standardised_data: 322 minutes per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices; about 5.4 hours).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard. The annual figure is roughly one-twelfth of the FY 2023-24 annual figure (3,929 minutes), which the licensee's return does not explain; see Source_Gaps G18.
rows.documentation: Monthly SAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration (column 9 of the SoP 011 table, hr:min converted to minutes) / customers served. Annual SAIDI = sum of the twelve monthly values. The return's annual 0:26 is a monthly average of the same quantity. Column 7 of the same table ('total customer interruption duration', Ri x Ni) totals 23,273,277:24, about 20% above column 9 (19,435,301:04); column 9 was used because it reproduces the printed monthly SAIDI and CAIDI. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 011 format)'.

rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) - licensee-wide, derived from SoP 010 and 011-B
rows.definition: Cumulative customer interruption duration divided by the total number of interrupted customers for sustained interruptions (CAIDI = SAIDI / SAIFI), derived from the licensee's reported SAIFI and SAIDI components.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; base/target indices to be set by the Commission (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: Reported monthly in the return (annual row 2.99 minutes per interruption, a monthly average).
rows.standardised_data: 2.53 minutes per interruption (derived from the reported SAIDI and SAIFI components).

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 010 format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-interruptions divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 010 reporting format (the definition in 2023 Reg. 5.2).
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: 12.28 interruptions per customer per month (monthly average as printed in the return).
rows.standardised_data: 147.93 interruptions per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard. The annual figure is about 16% above the FY 2024-25 annual figure (127.50) on the same compilation basis.
rows.documentation: The return's 12.28 is the total of the twelve monthly numerators divided by the total of the twelve monthly customer counts, a customer-weighted monthly average and not an annual value. Annual SAIFI = sum over months of (customer interruptions / customers served), each month with its own customer count. The monthly indices agree with the printed values to two decimals. October-December are labelled 'Oct-26', 'Nov-26' and 'Dec-26' in the SAIFI, SAIDI and MAIFI tables and 'Oct-25' etc. in the CAIDI table; they were read as October-December 2025. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 010 format)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) – Consumer-count basis, Licensee-wide, SoP 011 format
rows.definition: Annual sum of monthly customer-minutes of interruption divided by customers served, as compiled in the licensee's SoP 011 reporting format.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; the Commission is to set targets (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: 24.9 minutes per customer per month (monthly average; printed in the return as 0:25 hr:min).
rows.standardised_data: 299 minutes per customer (sum of the 12 monthly indices; about 5.0 hours).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard. The annual figure is about 7% below the FY 2024-25 figure (322 minutes) on the same compilation basis.
rows.documentation: Monthly SAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration (column 9 of the SoP 011 table, hr:min converted to minutes) / customers served as stated in the same table. Annual SAIDI = sum of the twelve monthly values. The return's annual 0:25 is a monthly average of the same quantity. Customer counts in the SoP 011 table for January-March 2026 (3,718,705; 3,717,386; 3,732,589) differ from those in the SoP 010 table (about 3,805,000); each table's own counts were used. Column 7 of the table (Ri x Ni) differs from column 9; column 9 was used because it reproduces the printed monthly SAIDI. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) - licensee-wide, customer-count basis (SoP 011 format)'.

rows.reported_data: 18.41 momentary interruptions per customer per month (monthly average as printed in the return).

rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the reported figure is licensee-wide and customer-count based, not segregated by urban, rural and agricultural feeders.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard.
rows.documentation: The return's 18.41 is the total of the twelve monthly numerators divided by the total of the twelve monthly customer counts, a monthly average. rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) - licensee-wide, derived from SoP 010 and 011-B
rows.definition: Cumulative customer interruption duration divided by the total number of interrupted customers for sustained interruptions (CAIDI = SAIDI / SAIFI), derived from the licensee's reported SAIFI and SAIDI components.
rows.standard: No numerical target specified in the Regulations; base/target indices to be set by the Commission (2023 Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: Reported monthly in the return (annual row 2.36 minutes per interruption, a monthly average).
rows.standardised_data: 2.02 minutes per interruption (derived from the reported SAIDI and SAIFI components).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations specify no numerical target, and the annual value is derived from reported SAIDI and SAIFI components.
rows.interpretation: No benchmark exists in the Regulations, so the index cannot be compared with a standard.
rows.documentation: CAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration / total customer interruptions (2023 Reg. 5.2), computed over the whole year as the ratio of totals: customer-minutes 1,103,416,776 (SoP 011) divided by customer interruptions 547,126,701 (SoP 010). The return prints monthly CAIDI as printed SAIDI / printed SAIFI; the recomputed monthly values differ from the printed ones by at most 0.22 minute. | Unit added: minutes per interruption. Basis: MGVCL Calculations file (Unit_Evidence sheet) shows the return's CAIDI column is printed in minutes (SAIDI/SAIFI); minutes is the CAIDI unit throughout the dataset. Value unchanged.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI)
rows.definition: Average duration of sustained interruptions per consumer in the reporting period: sum of (restoration time in minutes x consumers interrupted) divided by total consumers. Scheduled outages, outages of 5 minutes or less, grid failures and Regulation 26.1 events are excluded; agricultural feeders are excluded in the return.
rows.standard: No numerical benchmark specified (Reg. 22.12.4: standards fixed by the Commission from time to time).
rows.standardised_data: Annual value from the twelve monthly figures (Apr-25 to Mar-26): 1716.65 minutes per consumer.
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations do not specify a numerical benchmark for this index (Regulation 22.12.4 refers to standards of reliability fixed by the Commission from time to time; none was identified for FY 2025-26).
rows.interpretation: No quantitative regulatory benchmark is specified for direct comparison.
rows.documentation: Annual value: sum of the twelve monthly sums of restoration time x consumers interrupted, divided by the mean of the twelve monthly consumer counts; monthly values were not averaged. rows.standard: No numerical benchmark specified (Reg. 22.12.4: standards fixed by the Commission from time to time).
rows.reported_data: Monthly, interruptions per consumer: Apr-25 3.18; May-25 4.61; Jun-25 2.51; Jul-25 1.57; Aug-25 3.00; Sep-25 3.03; Oct-25 2.00; Nov-25 2.82; Dec-25 2.57; Jan-26 2.00; Feb-26 1.43; Mar-26 1.75.
rows.standardised_data: Annual value from the twelve monthly figures (Apr-25 to Mar-26): 30.41 interruptions per consumer.
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations do not specify a numerical benchmark for this index (Regulation 22.12.4 refers to standards of reliability fixed by the Commission from time to time; none was identified for FY 2025-26).
rows.interpretation: No quantitative regulatory benchmark is specified for direct comparison.
rows.documentation: Annual value: sum of the twelve monthly consumer-interruption counts divided by the mean of the twelve monthly consumer counts; monthly values were not averaged. Monthly SAIFI ranges from 1.43 (Feb-26) to 4.61 (May-25). Monthly SAIFI was recomputed as Ni / Nt because one printed cell in the December return was stale; Oct-Mar values agree with S11. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) per connected consumer, computed for the DISCOM as a whole from monthly feeder data, reported separately for rural and urban feeders.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed; no numeric target in the regulation. Targets are to be notified annually by the Commission.
rows.reported_data: Reported annual SAIFI by feeder category (interruptions per consumer): JGY 96.64; urban 46.58; other 30.04.
rows.standardised_data: 68.86 interruptions per consumer per year (JGY, urban and other feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: No numeric target is prescribed in the regulation and no Commission-notified FY 2021-22 target was located, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: PGVCL's agricultural-dominant feeders show higher frequency (R04); no benchmark is available for the non-agricultural categories.
rows.documentation: Annual SAIFI recomputed as the sum of 12 monthly customer-interruption totals (SoP 011-A, column CI) for JGY, urban and other feeders divided by the average of the 12 monthly consumer counts. Agricultural-dominant feeders are excluded (R04). Monthly index values were not summed or averaged. Using the reported year-end consumer count instead gives 68.57. Detail in the calculations workbook (Annual_Indices). | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.

rows.indicator: Restoration of supply after routine line fault
rows.definition: Time to restore supply after a routine line fault.
rows.standard: Urban: within 8 working hours. Rural: within 24 hours.
rows.reported_data: Not reported as a rate; complaints are reported by class and timeliness band only.
rows.standardised_data: 99.5% of complaints in class A(ii) interruption due to line breakdown were redressed within the stipulated time (annual).
rows.why_not_comparable: The compliance report gives complaint counts by class and by whether they were redressed in the stipulated time, not event-level times, and does not split urban and rural cases. The time standard therefore cannot be tested case by case.
rows.interpretation: Most complaints in this class were redressed within the stipulated time; the standard cannot be tested for individual cases.
rows.documentation: Annual share = complaints redressed within 50% of the stipulated time plus within the stipulated time, divided by all complaints redressed in the class, summed over the four quarterly registers. Quarterly shares were not averaged. The class is an Appendix-B complaint classification and is matched to this indicator by subject; the stipulated time in the register is not split into urban and rural cases. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: Billing complaint resolution
rows.definition: Time to resolve billing complaints.
rows.standard: Arithmetical errors, non-receipt or inadequate payment time: same day if in person, on day of acknowledgement if by post. Other cases: within 10 days. Where a site visit is needed: within 15 days.
rows.reported_data: Not reported as a rate; complaints are reported by class and timeliness band only.
rows.standardised_data: 98.8% of complaints in class E(i) and E(ii) bills were redressed within the stipulated time (annual).
rows.why_not_comparable: The compliance report gives complaint counts by class and by whether they were redressed in the stipulated time, not event-level times, and does not split urban and rural cases. The time standard therefore cannot be tested case by case.
rows.interpretation: Most complaints in this class were redressed within the stipulated time; the standard cannot be tested for individual cases.
rows.documentation: Annual share = complaints redressed within 50% of the stipulated time plus within the stipulated time, divided by all complaints redressed in the class, summed over the four quarterly registers. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) per connected consumer, computed for the DISCOM as a whole from monthly feeder data, reported separately for rural and urban feeders.
rows.standard: Applies in both periods (2005 Regs Cl. 7.1(a), 7.2, 7.4; 2023 Regs Cl. 5.1-5.2, 5.4). 2005 text: Index and formula prescribed; no numeric target in the regulation. Targets are to be notified annually by the Commission. 2023 text: SAIFI per IEEE 1366-2003, monthly, 11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural; momentary interruptions are 5 minutes or less; scheduled outages, grid failures and force-majeure outages are excluded. Base/target indices to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported yearly SAIFI by feeder category (interruptions per consumer): JGY 95.04; urban 55.88; other 50.91.
rows.standardised_data: 75.03 interruptions per consumer per year (JGY, urban and other feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (2023 Regulations Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2023-24, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: PGVCL's agricultural-dominant feeders show higher frequency (R04); no benchmark is available for the non-agricultural categories.
rows.documentation: Annual index recomputed from the sum of 12 monthly component totals divided by the average of the 12 monthly consumer counts, using the 12 monthly components for JGY, urban and other feeders combined (agricultural-dominant feeders are shown at R04). Monthly or quarterly index values were not summed or averaged. PGVCL's category consumer counts shifted in October 2023 (agricultural-dominant fell by about 128,000, JGY and urban rose), which affects category-level comparisons with earlier years; the combined non-agricultural count is less affected. Using the March consumer count, as PGVCL does for its yearly figures, gives 73.61. The 2023 Regulations also exclude scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages; the report does not state whether these were excluded. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.

rows.standard: Applies in both periods (2005 Regs Cl. 6.3(a)-(c); 2023 Regs Cl. 4.19). 2005 text: Low voltage: +6% / -6%. High voltage: +6% / -9%. Extra high voltage: +10% / -12.5%. 2023 text: Low voltage +6%/-6%; high voltage +6%/-9%; extra high voltage +10%/-12.5%.
rows.reported_data: Share of sampled supply points outside the voltage limits: low voltage 0%; high voltage 0%; extra high voltage 0%.

rows.interpretation: No sampled supply point fell outside the prescribed voltage limits. The result is a sample test and does not cover all consumers.
rows.documentation: Taken as reported; no transformation. The limits are the same in the 2005 and 2023 Regulations. Sample sizes were 931 (low voltage), 163 (high voltage) and 16 (extra high voltage). PGVCL's sheet states limits of +/-6% (high voltage) and +/-10% (extra high voltage), narrower than the regulations' +6%/-9% and +10%/-12.5%; zero deviations against the narrower limits imply none outside the regulation limits. The '% compliance' column is calculated as deviations x 100 / sample and is read as the share outside limits. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.standard: Applies in both periods (2005 Regs Cl. 6.4-6.6; 2023 Regs Cl. 5.15-5.18). 2005 text: As specified in the Grid Connectivity Standards applicable to distribution systems (incorporated technical standard; limits not stated in the regulation). 2023 text: As specified in the Grid Connectivity Standards applicable to distribution systems.
rows.reported_data: Share of sampled consumers outside the harmonic limit stated in the report (3.5): HT consumers 10.1%; EHT consumers 0%. No LT samples reported.
rows.standardised_data: 10.1% of sampled HT consumers outside the stated limit; 0% of sampled EHT consumers (sample test; not annualised).
rows.why_not_comparable: Both regulations refer to the harmonic limits in the Grid Connectivity Standards; the applicable limit was not traced, so the 3.5 limit stated in PGVCL's sheet cannot be confirmed as the regulatory standard. The sheet's circle and PGVCL figures are identical to those in PGVCL's FY 2022-23 report.
rows.interpretation: No comparison with the regulatory standard can be drawn; the possibility that the sheet repeats the previous year's results has not been resolved.
rows.documentation: Share = deviations x 100 / sample, as in the report (8 of 79 HT samples; 0 of 1 EHT sample). The limit unit is not stated in the sheet.

rows.indicator_family: New connection - supply from existing network
rows.indicator: Release of new connection from existing network – Domestic and non-domestic
rows.definition: Time to release the connection after receipt of demand note amount and completion of formalities.
rows.standard: Until 5 Dec 2023 (2005 Regulations, Cl. 9.2): Within 20 days. Where mains extension or new substation is needed: within 2 months (urban) or 4 months (rural) of demand note amount. From 6 Dec 2023 (2023 Regulations, Cl. 4.2): After full payment of the demand note: from existing network, 7 days (urban) or 10 days (rural); with network modification: LT line up to 150 m, 15 days; LT line over 150 m or transformer augmentation, 21 days; new distribution transformer, 30 days; new HT line and transformer, 90 days; EHT line or sub-station, 180 days. Applies in urban and rural areas.
rows.reported_data: Not reported as a rate; complaints are reported by class and timeliness band, by quarter.
rows.standardised_data: 99.7% of complaints in class F(i) and F(ii) service connections were redressed within the stipulated time (annual, four quarters combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard changed on 6 Dec 2023 (2005 Regulations to 2023 Regulations) and reported data are not separated by regulatory period, so a single like-for-like comparison cannot be made. The compliance report also gives complaint counts by class and timeliness band, not event-level times, and does not split urban and rural cases.
rows.interpretation: Most complaints in this class were redressed within the stipulated time; the standard cannot be tested for individual cases.
rows.documentation: Annual share = complaints redressed within 50% of the stipulated time plus within the stipulated time, divided by all complaints redressed in the class (four timeliness bands), summed over the four quarterly registers (PGVCL total blocks). Quarterly shares were not averaged. The class is an Appendix-B complaint classification matched to this indicator by subject; the stipulated time is not split into urban and rural cases and is not stated for the period after 6 Dec 2023. Classes F(i) and F(ii) are combined. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'New connection (domestic and non-domestic): release of connection'.

rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average time required to restore service per interrupted consumer: cumulative customer interruption duration divided by the number of interrupted customers (sustained interruptions), computed monthly for the DISCOM as a whole.
rows.standard: No applicable standard before 6 Dec 2023. Index prescribed in the 2023 Regulations; no numeric target in the Regulations (base/target indices to be set by separate Commission guidelines or order).

rows.why_not_comparable: No applicable standard existed before 6 Dec 2023 and the Regulations set no numeric CAIDI target; the Commission's base/target indices (Cl. 5.4) were not located.
rows.interpretation: Average restoration time per interrupted consumer is longer on agricultural-dominant feeders. No benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: CAIDI = annual cumulative customer interruption duration divided by annual customer interruptions (SAIDI/SAIFI on the same components), in minutes; it does not depend on the consumer count. Computed from the SoP 011 monthly components; not a figure reported by PGVCL. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) per connected consumer, computed for the DISCOM as a whole from monthly feeder data, excluding scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed (IEEE 1366-2003); no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported SAIFI per month, quarterly and year (average monthly basis). JGY: 12.98, 19.04, 9.29, 8.39; year 12.41. Other than agricultural and JGY: 5.17, 7.20, 3.79, 4.56; year 5.18.
rows.standardised_data: 101.35 interruptions per consumer per year (JGY and other-than-agricultural feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2024-25, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Frequency is highest in the second quarter (July-September 2024) in every category. No benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: Annual index = sum of the four quarterly component totals divided by the average monthly consumer count (the four quarterly consumer-count sums, each the total of three monthly counts, added and divided by 12). Quarterly data are the most granular series in the report. PGVCL's own 'yearly' and quarterly index values are averages per month (total interruptions divided by the sum of monthly consumer counts) and were not summed or averaged. Non-agricultural = JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders; agricultural-dominant feeders are at R05. Scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages are excluded by the Regulations; the report does not state whether they were excluded. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.
rows.applicable_regulation: Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standards of Performance of Distribution Licensees) Regulations, 2023 (Notification No. 2 of 2023; Gujarat Government Gazette Extraordinary No. 108, Part IV-C, 06-12-2023)

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Total duration of sustained interruptions for the average connected consumer, computed as for SAIFI.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed (IEEE 1366-2003); no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported SAIDI per month, quarterly and year (minutes, average monthly basis). JGY: 728 minutes, 928 minutes, 437 minutes, 387 minutes; year 619 minutes. Other than agricultural and JGY: 273 minutes, 312 minutes, 159 minutes, 190 minutes; year 233 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: 4,891.2 minutes per consumer per year (JGY and other-than-agricultural feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2024-25, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Duration is highest in the second quarter in every category. No benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: SAIDI is lower-confidence: the report's own duration column is inconsistent with its reported SAIDI (see G07). Annual SAIDI uses cumulative customer-interruption duration rebuilt as quarterly reported SAIDI (hours:minutes) x the quarter's consumer-count sum, because the report's cumulative-duration column prints as overflow; rounding to the nearest minute limits the error to well under 0.1%. Annual SAIDI = sum of the four quarterly component totals divided by the average monthly consumer count (the four quarterly consumer-count sums, each the total of three monthly counts, added and divided by 12). Non-agricultural = JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders. | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours:minutes (hh:mm) to minutes for consistency across all DISCOMs and states (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '12:08' -> '728 minutes'; '15:28' -> '928 minutes'; '7:17' -> '437 minutes'; '6:27' -> '387 minutes'; '10:19' -> '619 minutes'; '4:33' -> '273 minutes'; '5:12' -> '312 minutes'; '2:39' -> '159 minutes'; '3:10' -> '190 minutes'; '3:53' -> '233 minutes'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIDI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.
