rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average time to restore service per interrupted consumer: cumulative customer interruption duration divided by number of interrupted customers (SAIDI/SAIFI). Also to be computed separately for HT consumers from metering data.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed; no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported CAIDI (minutes): JGY 4 minutes; other than agricultural and JGY 6 minutes (year).
rows.standardised_data: 48.3 minutes per interrupted consumer (JGY and other-than-agricultural feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2024-25, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Average restoration time per interrupted consumer is much longer than the figures PGVCL reports for CAIDI; no benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: CAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration / cumulative customer interruptions (the same components as SAIDI and SAIFI), in minutes; it does not depend on the consumer count. PGVCL's CAIDI sheet reports 0:03-0:16 hours:minutes, which does not agree with its own SAIDI/SAIFI (for the whole system, SAIDI 12:37 / SAIFI 12.03 is about 63 minutes), so the reported CAIDI values were not used. SAIDI is lower-confidence: the report's own duration column is inconsistent with its reported SAIDI (see G07). Annual SAIDI uses cumulative customer-interruption duration rebuilt as quarterly reported SAIDI (hours:minutes) x the quarter's consumer-count sum, because the report's cumulative-duration column prints as overflow; rounding to the nearest minute limits the error to well under 0.1%.  | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours:minutes (hh:mm) to minutes for consistency across all DISCOMs and states (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '0:04' -> '4 minutes'; '0:06' -> '6 minutes'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'CAIDI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.

rows.reported_data: Agricultural-dominant feeders. SAIFI per month by quarter: 27.95, 37.64, 24.12, 19.65 (yearly SAIFI blank in the report). SAIDI (minutes): 2,410 minutes, 3,734 minutes, 1,688 minutes, 1,185 minutes; year 2,250 minutes. MAIFI: 28.27, 33.16, 26.20, 24.31; year 27.97.
rows.standardised_data: SAIFI 327.72; SAIDI 26,993.0 minutes; MAIFI 335.64 per consumer per year; CAIDI 82.4 minutes per interrupted consumer.
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2024-25, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Agricultural-dominant feeders record the highest frequency and duration among PGVCL's feeder categories. No benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: Same method as R01-R04 for the agricultural-dominant category. SAIDI is lower-confidence: the report's own duration column is inconsistent with its reported SAIDI (see G07). Annual SAIDI uses cumulative customer-interruption duration rebuilt as quarterly reported SAIDI (hours:minutes) x the quarter's consumer-count sum, because the report's cumulative-duration column prints as overflow; rounding to the nearest minute limits the error to well under 0.1%. Annual index = sum of the four quarterly component totals divided by the average monthly consumer count (the four quarterly consumer-count sums, each the total of three monthly counts, added and divided by 12). Quarterly data are the most granular series in the report. PGVCL's own 'yearly' and quarterly index values are averages per month (total interruptions divided by the sum of monthly consumer counts) and were not summed or averaged.  | Unit conversion: Reported data converted from hours:minutes (hh:mm) to minutes for consistency across all DISCOMs and states (the unit used for this indicator throughout the dataset). Original values: '40:10' -> '2,410 minutes'; '62:14' -> '3,734 minutes'; '28:08' -> '1,688 minutes'; '19:45' -> '1,185 minutes'; '37:30' -> '2,250 minutes'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) per connected consumer, computed for the DISCOM as a whole from monthly feeder data, excluding scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed (IEEE 1366-2003); no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported SAIFI per month (average monthly basis), by quarter and year. JGY: Q1 15.88, Q2 15.92, Q3 10.80, Q4 7.48; year 12.48. Other than agricultural and JGY: Q1 5.52, Q2 4.77, Q3 3.75, Q4 3.43; year 4.36.
rows.standardised_data: 96.18 interruptions per consumer per year (JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2025-26, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Frequency is highest in the first half of the year (April-September 2025) and lowest in the fourth quarter. No benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: Annual index = sum of the 12 monthly component totals divided by the average of the 12 monthly consumer counts (monthly data are the most granular series in the report). PGVCL's own monthly, quarterly and 'yearly' index values are averages per month (interruptions divided by the sum of monthly consumer counts) and were not summed or averaged. Non-agricultural = JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders; agricultural-dominant feeders are at R05. Scheduled outages, grid failure and force-majeure outages are excluded by the Regulations; the report does not state whether they were excluded. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'SAIFI (11 kV/33 kV feeders excl. predominantly agricultural)'.

rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Total duration of sustained interruptions for the average connected consumer, computed as for SAIFI.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed (IEEE 1366-2003); no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported SAIDI per month (minutes, average monthly basis), by quarter and year. JGY: Q1 833 minutes, Q2 575 minutes, Q3 384 minutes, Q4 310 minutes; year 524 minutes. Other than agricultural and JGY: Q1 327 minutes, Q2 169 minutes, Q3 155 minutes, Q4 138 minutes; year 196 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: 4,124.8 minutes per consumer per year (JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2025-26, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.

rows.documentation: Annual SAIDI uses monthly customer-interruption duration rebuilt as reported monthly SAIDI (hours:minutes) x that month's consumer count, summed over 12 months. The level is consistent with FY 2024-25 but the duration inconsistency is unresolved (see Gaps_and_Decisions). rows.indicator: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) – 11 kV/33 kV feeders, Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average time to restore service per interrupted consumer: cumulative customer interruption duration divided by number of interrupted customers (SAIDI/SAIFI). Also to be computed separately for HT consumers from metering data.
rows.standard: Index and formula prescribed; no numeric target in the Regulations. Base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order.
rows.reported_data: Reported CAIDI (minutes), by quarter and year. JGY: Q1 4 minutes, Q2 3 minutes, Q3 4 minutes, Q4 3 minutes; year 3 minutes. Other than agricultural and JGY: Q1 6 minutes, Q2 5 minutes, Q3 10 minutes, Q4 6 minutes; year 7 minutes.
rows.standardised_data: 42.9 minutes per interrupted consumer (JGY plus 'other than Ag & JGY' feeders combined).
rows.why_not_comparable: The Regulations prescribe the index but no numeric target; the Commission is to set base/target indices by separate guidelines or order (Cl. 5.4) and none was located for FY 2025-26, so the reported index cannot be tested against a standard.
rows.interpretation: Computed average time per interrupted consumer is much longer than the figures PGVCL reports for CAIDI; no benchmark is available.
rows.documentation: CAIDI = cumulative customer interruption duration / cumulative customer interruptions, in minutes, from the same components as SAIDI and SAIFI (it does not depend on the consumer count). PGVCL's CAIDI sheet is not consistent with its own SAIDI and SAIFI (for the whole system, SAIDI 11:20 / SAIFI 13.23 is about 51 minutes against reported 0:08-0:12), contains entries such as 0.01 and 0.00 in October 2025 to February 2026, and shows consumer-count entries that do not match the other sheets, so the reported CAIDI values were not used. Annual SAIDI uses monthly customer-interruption duration rebuilt as reported monthly SAIDI (hours:minutes) x that month's consumer count, summed over 12 months. The report's duration columns (customer interruption duration, cumulative duration) are inconsistent with its reported SAIDI and with each other (for April 2025 the duration column gives about 1.0 hour per consumer against reported SAIDI of 10:46) and mix decimal-day and hours:minutes formats, so the reported SAIDI column was used; its yearly figure (11:20) is reproduced by this method. rows.indicator: Restoration of supply after HT/drop-out fuse fault
rows.definition: Time taken to restore supply after a no-power complaint caused by an HT/DO fuse fault, measured from receipt of the complaint (faults not due to a line fault or transformer failure).
rows.standard: Within 6 hours in urban areas; within 24 hours in rural areas (Reg. 5.1).
rows.reported_data: Share of complaints redressed within the stipulated time (Loose connections from pole): 99.99%
rows.standardised_data: 99.99% (annual register total; no annualisation required)
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard sets a time limit for each case, while the return reports only the share of all complaints in the category 'Loose connections from pole' redressed within the licensee's stipulated time; that category covers more than this one standard and does not show the time taken for each case.
rows.interpretation: UGVCL reported that 99.99% of complaints in the category 'Loose connections from pole' were redressed within the stipulated time in FY 2021-22. Compliance with this specific standard cannot be determined from the category share.
rows.documentation: Share = complaints redressed within 50% of the stipulated time plus those within the stipulated time, divided by total complaints in classification A(i) of the annual complaints register (SoP 003 B); this follows the register's grouping of 'in stipulated time'. The register is an annual total for FY 2021-22. The classification is mapped to this row by subject matter; See sheet 'Register_003B'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – All feeder categories
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions (longer than 5 minutes) per consumer served, computed monthly for the licensee as a whole; the Regulations require stacking of 11 kV/33 kV feeders excluding predominantly agricultural feeders, reported separately for urban and rural feeders (Reg. 7.2).
rows.standard: Index to be computed and reported monthly under IEEE Standard 1366 as specified in Reg. 7.1(a) and 7.2; numerical target levels to be notified annually by the Commission (Reg. 7.4).
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer), Apr-22 to Mar-23: Apr-22 1.49; May-22 1.70; Jun-22 2.84; Jul-22 3.38; Aug-22 2.82; Sep-22 2.68; Oct-22 1.69; Nov-22 1.31; Dec-22 1.43; Jan-23 2.03; Feb-23 1.17; Mar-23 2.20
rows.standardised_data: 24.74 interruptions per consumer for FY 2022-23 (sum of monthly values)
rows.why_not_comparable: No numerical target level for FY 2022-23 was located (Reg. 7.4 provides for annual target levels to be notified by the Commission), so there is no benchmark to compare the reported index with.
rows.interpretation: For FY 2022-23, UGVCL reported an annual SAIFI of 24.74 interruptions per consumer for all feeder categories of UGVCL. No benchmark is available for comparison.
rows.documentation: Annual value = sum of the twelve monthly indices, each calculated as monthly total (customer interruptions, customer-hours or customer momentary interruptions) divided by the customers served in that month, from the monthly components in the return; no estimation of missing months was needed. The return counts consumers whereas Reg. 7.2 weights by connected load, and it does not split urban and rural feeders; this series covers all feeder categories including agricultural feeders, whereas Reg. 7.2 excludes predominantly agricultural feeders. See Calculations workbook, sheet 'Rel_ALL'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. rows.indicator: Disposal of consumer grievances by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum
rows.definition: Time taken by the Forum to pass an order on a grievance, from receipt of the grievance.
rows.standard: Within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the grievance (Reg. 2.47); order within 30 days of filing for other grievances (Reg. 2.48).
rows.reported_data: Share of grievances decided within 30 days, by quarter - Q1: Mehsana forum 100.00%, Ahmedabad forum 100.00%; Q2: Mehsana forum 80.00%, Ahmedabad forum 100.00% (Q3 and Q4 not available)
rows.standardised_data: Not annualised: Q3 and Q4 of FY 2022-23 were not available in the official publications reviewed.
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard applies to each grievance (an order within 30 days of receipt; 7 days for disconnection cases), while only quarterly shares of grievances decided within 30 days are published, and only for the first two quarters of the year, so compliance for each grievance and for the year cannot be tested.
rows.interpretation: For April to September 2022, UGVCL's two grievance forums decided between 80.00% and 100.00% of grievances within 30 days in each forum and quarter. Compliance for each grievance and for the full year cannot be determined.
rows.documentation: Quarterly forum shares = grievances decided within 30 days divided by grievances decided in the quarter. No annual share was constructed because two quarters are missing; no missing period was estimated and percentages were not averaged. See the Calculations workbook, sheets 'CGRF_Data' and 'CGRF_Calc'.

rows.indicator_family: Opening of neutral / neutral voltage complaint
rows.indicator: Neutral voltage at consumer premises
rows.definition: Neutral voltage at the consumer's supply as a share of the supply voltage.
rows.standard: Until 5 December 2023 (SoP Regulations 2005): Neutral voltage not to exceed 2% of the supply voltage (Reg. 6.1(a)).
rows.reported_data: Share of sampled consumers with neutral voltage above 2%: Domestic 2.12%; Commercial 1.65%; Industrial 0.86%; Agricultural 2.92%; Public water works 1.85%; HT industrial 0.47%
rows.standardised_data: 2.22% of all sampled consumers (all categories combined)
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard applies to the neutral voltage at each consumer's supply, while only the share of a sample of consumers whose measured neutral voltage exceeded 2% is reported, so compliance at each consumer's supply cannot be tested. The return reports the whole year and does not separate 6 December 2023 to 31 March 2024, when the 2023 Regulations applied; the 2005 standard applied only until 5 December 2023.
rows.interpretation: UGVCL's sample tests for FY 2023-24 found neutral voltage above 2% at 2.22% of sampled consumers. Whether supply at all consumers met the standard cannot be determined from a sample share.
rows.documentation: Category shares are sample deviations divided by sample size, as in the return; the combined share was calculated from combined sample counts, not by averaging category percentages. 'Deviation of results from the sample test' is read as the number of samples exceeding the 2% limit. The sample is not stated to be representative. See sheet 'Sample_Tests'.

rows.indicator: Disposal of consumer grievances by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum
rows.definition: Time taken by the Forum to pass an order on a grievance, from receipt of the grievance.
rows.standard: Within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the grievance (Reg. 2.47); order within 30 days of filing for other grievances (Reg. 2.48).
rows.reported_data: Share of grievances decided within 30 days, by quarter - Q1: Mehsana forum 100.00%, Ahmedabad forum 55.56%; Q2: Mehsana forum 100.00%, Ahmedabad forum 100.00%; Q3: Mehsana forum 100.00%, Ahmedabad forum 70.00%; Q4: Mehsana forum 70.00%, Ahmedabad forum 80.00%
rows.standardised_data: 81.67% of grievances decided within 30 days, both UGVCL forums combined (Mehsana forum 87.50%; Ahmedabad forum 77.78%)
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard applies to each grievance (an order within 30 days of receipt; 7 days for disconnection cases), while only the share of grievances decided within 30 days is published, so compliance of each grievance cannot be tested.
rows.interpretation: In FY 2023-24, 81.67% of the grievances decided by UGVCL's two grievance redressal forums were decided within 30 days; the quarterly share ranged from 55.56% to 100.00% across the two forums. Whether each grievance met the standard cannot be determined from this share.
rows.documentation: Quarterly forum shares = grievances decided within 30 days divided by grievances decided in the quarter, from the eight quarterly forum reports. The annual shares were built from the summed counts of the four quarters (and, for the combined figure, of both forums); percentages were not averaged. The Ahmedabad tables were recovered from text in which column alignment was lost, and each quarter was checked against the table's own arithmetic. See the Calculations workbook, sheets 'CGRF_Data', 'CGRF_Calc' and 'Checks'.

rows.reported_data: Share of sampled consumers with harmonic distortion above the limit: LT consumers 0.21%; HT consumers 1.64%; EHT consumers 0.00%

rows.definition: Time taken by the Forum to pass an order on a grievance, from receipt of the grievance.
rows.standard: Within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the grievance (Reg. 2.47); order within 30 days of filing for other grievances (Reg. 2.48).

rows.why_not_comparable: The standard applies to each grievance (an order within 30 days of receipt; 7 days for disconnection cases), while only quarterly shares of grievances decided within 30 days are published, and only for part of the year, so compliance for each grievance and for the year cannot be tested.

The Ahmedabad and Mehsana tables were recovered from text in which column alignment was lost; each quarter was checked against the table's own arithmetic. rows.indicator: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) – Excluding agricultural feeders
rows.definition: Average number of sustained interruptions per consumer in a month, computed for the DISCOM as a whole by stacking all 11 kV/33 kV feeders other than predominantly agricultural feeders (IEEE 1366).
rows.standard: Throughout FY 2025-26 (SoP Regulations 2023): Index to be computed monthly under Reg. 5.1-5.2 (IEEE Standard 1366-2003); no numerical level is set in the Regulations - base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order (Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: Monthly SAIFI (interruptions per consumer) computed from the return's JGY and other-feeder components, Apr-25 to Mar-26: Apr-25 2.58; May-25 8.33; Jun-25 6.02; Jul-25 8.05; Aug-25 8.18; Sep-25 8.38; Oct-25 4.86; Nov-25 3.73; Dec-25 3.61; Jan-26 4.16; Feb-26 1.88; Mar-26 4.41
rows.standardised_data: 64.18 interruptions per consumer for FY 2025-26 (sum of monthly values)
rows.why_not_comparable: No numerical target level for FY 2025-26 was located (Reg. 5.4 of the 2023 Regulations leaves targets to a separate Commission order), so there is no benchmark to compare the reported index with.
rows.interpretation: For FY 2025-26, the annual SAIFI calculated from UGVCL's monthly components is 64.18 interruptions per consumer for feeders other than agriculture-dominant feeders (JGY and other feeders) of UGVCL. No benchmark is available for comparison.
rows.documentation: Annual value = sum of the twelve monthly indices (CAIDI: annual SAIDI divided by annual SAIFI), each monthly index calculated as the monthly total (customer interruptions, customer-hours or customer momentary interruptions) divided by the customers served in that month, from the components in the return; no month was estimated. The return does not publish a series for feeders other than agriculture-dominant feeders; it was built by adding the JGY and other-feeder counts (the return's whole-company series equals the sum of its three categories exactly), then dividing by the combined customers served. The return counts consumers whereas Reg. 5.2 refers to feeders at 11 kV/33 kV and does not state the weighting; the return does not split urban and rural feeders. The return's 'Total' rows are averages across months and were not used. See Calculations workbook, sheet 'Rel_NAG'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) - feeders other than agriculture-dominant'.

rows.standard: Throughout FY 2025-26 (SoP Regulations 2023): Index to be computed monthly under Reg. 5.1-5.2 (IEEE Standard 1366-2003); no numerical level is set in the Regulations - base/target indices are to be set by the Commission through separate guidelines or order (Reg. 5.4).
rows.reported_data: Monthly MAIFI (momentary interruptions per consumer) computed from the return's JGY and other-feeder components, Apr-25 to Mar-26: Apr-25 5.39; May-25 10.05; Jun-25 9.14; Jul-25 9.48; Aug-25 10.66; Sep-25 9.77; Oct-25 7.10; Nov-25 5.63; Dec-25 5.53; Jan-26 6.08; Feb-26 2.38; Mar-26 4.00
rows.standardised_data: 85.22 momentary interruptions per consumer for FY 2025-26 (sum of monthly values)
rows.why_not_comparable: No numerical target level for FY 2025-26 was located (Reg. 5.4 of the 2023 Regulations leaves targets to a separate Commission order), so there is no benchmark to compare the reported index with.
rows.interpretation: For FY 2025-26, the annual MAIFI calculated from UGVCL's monthly components is 85.22 momentary interruptions per consumer for feeders other than agriculture-dominant feeders (JGY and other feeders) of UGVCL. No benchmark is available for comparison.
rows.documentation: Annual value = sum of the twelve monthly indices (CAIDI: annual SAIDI divided by annual SAIFI), each monthly index calculated as the monthly total (customer interruptions, customer-hours or customer momentary interruptions) divided by the customers served in that month, from the components in the return; no month was estimated. The return does not publish a series for feeders other than agriculture-dominant feeders; it was built by adding the JGY and other-feeder counts (the return's whole-company series equals the sum of its three categories exactly), then dividing by the combined customers served. The return counts consumers whereas Reg. 5.2 refers to feeders at 11 kV/33 kV and does not state the weighting; the return does not split urban and rural feeders. The return's 'Total' rows are averages across months and were not used. See Calculations workbook, sheet 'Rel_NAG'. | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states. Original name: 'Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index (MAIFI) - feeders other than agriculture-dominant'.

rows.definition: Time taken to enquire into any other complaint (including complaints of a recurring nature).
rows.standard: Throughout FY 2025-26 (SoP Regulations 2023): Within 10 days of the complaint (Reg. 5.14).
rows.reported_data: Share of complaints redressed within the stipulated time (Others): 97.80%
rows.standardised_data: 97.80% (annual register total; no annualisation required)

rows.indicator: Voltage and current harmonic distortion
rows.definition: Voltage and current harmonic distortion at consumers' premises, assessed by sample compliance tests (Appendix D, SoP 009).
rows.standard: Throughout FY 2025-26 (SoP Regulations 2023): Limits as specified by the Authority in the Grid Connectivity Standards applicable to distribution systems (Reg. 5.18); Appendix D, SoP 009 lists 3.5% for LT consumers, 3.0% for HT consumers and 3.0% for EHT consumers.
rows.reported_data: Share of sampled consumers with harmonic distortion above the limit: LT consumers 0.27%; HT consumers 2.39%; EHT consumers 0.00%
rows.standardised_data: 0.34% of all sampled consumers (all categories combined)
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard applies to the harmonic distortion at each consumer's installation, and its numerical limits are set by reference to CEA standards that were not reviewed, while only the share of a sample above UGVCL's applied limit is reported, so compliance cannot be tested.
rows.interpretation: UGVCL's sample tests for FY 2025-26 found harmonic distortion above its applied limit at 0.34% of sampled consumers. Compliance with the CEA-specified limits cannot be determined.
rows.documentation: The return applies limits of 3.50% (LT) and 3.00% (HT and EHT), as in the Appendix D format of the 2023 Regulations; they were not checked against the CEA Grid Connectivity Standards. The combined share was calculated from combined sample counts. The return does not say whether voltage or current distortion was measured. See sheet 'Sample_Tests'.

rows.reported_data: Share of complaints redressed within the stipulated time (Refund of amount due on temporary connection): 98.54%
rows.standardised_data: 98.54% (annual register total; no annualisation required)
rows.why_not_comparable: The standard sets a time limit for each case, while the return reports only the share of all complaints in the category 'Refund of amount due on temporary connection' redressed within the licensee's stipulated time; that category covers more than this one standard and does not show the time taken for each case.
rows.interpretation: UGVCL reported that 98.54% of complaints in the category 'Refund of amount due on temporary connection' were redressed within the stipulated time in FY 2025-26. Compliance with this specific standard cannot be determined from the category share.
rows.documentation: Share = complaints redressed within the stipulated time divided by total complaints in classification H of the annual complaints register (SoP 003 B, Appendix B format); the register is an annual total for FY 2025-26 and the classification is mapped to this row by subject matter using Appendix A of the 2023 Regulations. See sheet 'Register_003B'. The 2023 Regulations contain no corresponding deposit-refund clause; the Supply Code period (60 days) is the only standard carried (see Review List). | Indicator name standardised for consistency across all DISCOMs and states.
